title: Pre-flight preview card contradicts itself when the polar-alignment check is disabled
summary: _LivePreviewCard emitted a hard-coded per-strictness bullet list and then an independent polar-age bullet, so at polarAlignmentMaxAgeDays == 0 the same card said the run is blocked on 'stale polar alignment' AND that the polar-alignment age check is disabled. PolarAlignmentFreshnessRule.validate returns const [] when polarAlignmentMaxAgeDays <= 0 (preflight_rules.dart:601), so the strictness bullet was the false half. Replaced the hard-coded lists with a _gradedChecks getter composed from the live config ('stale polar alignment' only when polarAgeDays > 0), shared by all three modes. Two further false statements in the same card fell out of tracing the rules and were fixed with it: (a) Normal/Strict quoted 'time drift > 30s' when TimeSyncRule grades from warningThresholdSecs = 2 s upward and 30 s is the unconditional error, so the card understated what those modes flag; (b) Lax promised time drift 'becomes an info note' when TimeSyncRule explicitly refuses to degrade the >= 30 s error under any strictness -- Lax now states that outright.
revert_check: Restored the file to git HEAD (reverting the `if (polarAgeDays > 0) 'stale polar alignment'` conditional in _gradedChecks, the 2 s wording, and the Lax always-blocks bullet). 4 of 5 tests failed: 'strict preview drops polar alignment when the age check is off', 'normal preview drops polar alignment when the age check is off', 'lax preview does not promise that a >30s clock skew is advisory', 'graded-check wording matches the rule thresholds'. The 5th ('strict preview names polar alignment when the age check is on') is the positive control and correctly still passed. Restored -> 5/5 pass.
caveats: preflight_settings.dart sits just outside the literal ownership glob, but this findings file is the only one in reports/coverage/fix3/ that references it, so no concurrent agent owns it.

title: Image Grading: thresholds can be set outside the range the pipeline can measure, silently killing the check
summary: The eccentricity half of the finding (max 1.0) was ALREADY FIXED uncommitted in the working tree by an earlier wave (max 0.95 + explanatory copy) but had no test. Verified it, then found the cap was still one notch too loose and closed the rest of the class the finding named. (1) Eccentricity: detect_stars drops sources above DETECTION_MAX_ECCENTRICITY = 0.95 (stats.rs:166/235) so frame_eccentricity's median never exceeds 0.95, and image_grading rejects on `ecc > threshold` -- a threshold AT 0.95 is as dead as one above it. Field max is now 0.94, the largest firing value at the field's 2 decimals. (2) HFR absolute max was 50 px; calculate_image_hfr means the HFRs from detect_stars, each measured inside StarDetectionConfig.hfr_radius = 20 px, so no frame reports 50 and the gate could never fire. Max is now 20.0. (3) HFR absolute min was 0.1 px; detect_stars discards every source under StarDetectionConfig.min_hfr = 1.0 as a hot pixel (stats.rs:334), so 'reject if HFR > 0.1' rejects every frame that has stars. Min is now 1.0. (4) Clamping only guards NEW input -- a value persisted before the bounds existed (the audit itself wrote eccentricity 1.0 to the DB) still loads verbatim and renders as a normal armed threshold. Added _hfrInertNote / _eccentricityInertNote, appended to the row subtitle, which say in plain words that the stored value can never fire or rejects every frame.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/image_grading_settings_test.dart (10 tests, all pass; the pre-existing 'thresholds commit on submit and clamp the visible value' was updated from the old 50 px ceiling to 20 px)
revert_check: Reverted all three production call sites at once: `min: _hfrFloorPx, max: _hfrCeilingPx` -> `min: 0.1, max: 50.0`; `max: _eccentricityMaxInput` -> `max: 1.0`; and both `subtitle: _withNote(...)` wrappers back to the plain subtitle strings (severing the note wiring, not just the helper). 6 of 10 tests failed: 'thresholds commit on submit and clamp the visible value', 'eccentricity clamps to a value the detector can exceed', 'HFR clamps up to the floor the detector can report', 'a stored threshold past the measurable range says it is dead', 'an eccentricity threshold exactly at the ceiling is dead too', 'a stored threshold below the measurable range says so too'. 'a usable threshold carries no warning' is the negative control and correctly still passed. Restored -> 10/10 pass, and 15/15 with the preflight file.
caveats: Deliberately did NOT touch 'star count min' max 100000, which the finding also named. There is no code-level bound on detected star count (detect_stars has no cap; min_area 9 px over a 60 MP sensor bounds it in the millions), so any ceiling I picked would be a guess, and a guess set too low would block a legitimate config on a dense wide field -- the inverted-fix failure mode this campaign is watching for. The skotiq_core setters (settings_sections/image_grading.dart) still validate the full domain (HFR 0.1-50, eccentricity 0-1); that is the documented split ('the settings field is what caps operator input at the useful subrange') and that file is owned by a concurrent agent, so a headless/API caller can still store an inert value -- it will now at least be labelled dead when the settings screen renders it.
